Light-to-moderate rainfall on top of already saturated ground will
result in runoff and nuisance flooding.

* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...Central Mohave County in northwestern Arizona...

* WHEN...Until 1230 AM MST.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas.
Dangerous flows over low-water crossings. Some low-water crossings
may become impassable.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...

thunderstorms. Minor flooding is ongoing or expected to begin
shortly in the advisory area. Up to 0.5 inches of rain have
fallen.

over the area. This additional rain will result in minor
flooding.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Valentine, Peach Springs, Antares Road, Buck and Doe Road, and
Diamond Creek Campground.

...The National Weather Service in Amarillo has issued a Flood
Warning for the following rivers in Texas...

Canadian River at Amarillo 19N affecting Potter County.

For the Canadian River...including Amarillo 19N...Minor flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Canadian River at Amarillo 19N.

* WHEN...Until Thursday evening.

* IMPACTS...At 10.0 feet, Portions of Rosita Creek Flats Recreational
Area floods. Primitive campers and recreational vehicles are in
imminent danger. Dirt roads that lead to highway 287 from Rosita
Creek Flats are impassable.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 12:00 AM CDT Wednesday the stage was 6.5 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 7.0 feet.
- Forecast...The river will rise above flood stage early this
morning to 8.7 feet this afternoon. It will then fall below flood
stage late tomorrow morning to 6.4 feet Friday evening. It will
rise to 6.5 feet early Saturday afternoon. It will then fall
again and remain below flood stage.
- Flood stage is 7.0 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 8.2
feet on 05/19/2023.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

events.title: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
FFWEPZ

The National Weather Service in El Paso Tx/Santa Teresa has extended
the

* Flash Flood Warning for...
The Rio Grande between Rincon Arroyo and Leasburg Diversion Dam...
and Rincon Arroyo near Rincon.

* Until 130 AM MDT.

* At 1111 PM MDT, Water levels on the Rio Grande at Hayner's Bridge
continue to slowly drop. But flooding is still likely occurring
north of Leasburg Dam. Water levels are also continuing to drop at
Rincon Arroyo.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by heavy rain.

SOURCE...Gauges reported.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor
drainage and low-lying areas.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Rincon, Peaceful Valley, Selden Canyon, Rinconcito, and Radium
Springs north of Leasburg Dam.

The Rio Grande at Hayner's Bridge crested at 10.87 feet, with a flow
of 6,307 cfs, at 730 PM. It has since dropped to 10.17 feet and a
flow of 5,434 cfs as of 11 PM.

River levels continue to slowly rise at Leasburg Dam, but no flooding
is anticipated south of Leasburg due to levee protection, and higher
ground along the right bank.
